enonce_markdown: On a topographic map, the buildings of a village are arranged in a single line on both sides of a road. Which type of settlement pattern is shown?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Settlement patterns are named by the shape the buildings form: nucleated (compact cluster), linear (along a line), dispersed (scattered).

### Solution

Buildings strung along a road, river or railway form a linear settlement.

A nucleated settlement is a compact cluster around a centre, a dispersed settlement has isolated farms spread widely, and a planned grid settlement has regular blocks cut by streets at right angles.

enonce_markdown: On a map with north at the top, a hospital is at 52 E, 40 N and a market is at 56 E, 36 N. In which direction is the market from the hospital?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Compare the grid values: a larger easting is further east, a smaller northing is further south.

### Solution

The market has a higher easting (56 against 52), so it is to the east, and a lower northing (36 against 40), so it is to the south. It lies south-east of the hospital.

North-east and north-west would need a higher northing, and south-west would need a lower easting.

enonce_markdown: On a map with a contour interval of 25 m, a road starts on the 400 m contour and climbs, crossing six more contours in all before it reaches its highest point on the sixth of them. What is the height of the highest point of the road?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Height gained = number of contour intervals crossed x contour interval. Add it to the starting height.

### Solution

Six contours are crossed after the starting one, so the road climbs 6 x 25 = 150 m. Height = 400 + 150 = 550 m.

525 m counts only five intervals, 575 m counts seven, and 406 m adds the number of contours instead of multiplying by the interval.

enonce_markdown: On a topographic map, a flat area of swamp with very widely spaced contours has almost no buildings, although it lies beside a main road. Which is the best explanation?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Read relief from the contour spacing: wide spacing means gentle slopes, so a lack of settlement on such ground must have another cause, here drainage.

### Solution

Widely spaced contours show a gentle gradient, and the swamp symbol shows poor drainage and seasonal flooding. These make building, sanitation and farming difficult, so settlement avoids the swamp even though the road is close.

Steep slopes would show closely spaced contours, so that explanation contradicts the map. Dense contours and high altitude are not shown by widely spaced lines.

choix.texte: The slopes are too steep for houses.
The land is so high that temperatures are too low for settlement.
Poor drainage and flooding make building and farming difficult.
Closely spaced contours make road access impossible.

enonce_markdown: A rectangular plantation on a 1:50,000 map measures 3.2 cm by 2.4 cm. (a) Calculate the real area in square kilometres and in hectares. (b) State two map features that would help you to explain why the plantation is located there.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Convert each map length to a ground length with the scale, then multiply. 1 km2 = 100 hectares.

### Solution

(a) 3.2 cm x 50,000 = 160,000 cm = 1.6 km; 2.4 cm x 50,000 = 120,000 cm = 1.2 km. Area = 1.6 x 1.2 = 1.92 km2 = 192 hectares.

(b) Two relevant features: a road or railway nearby for the evacuation of the produce; gentle slopes shown by widely spaced contours that allow mechanisation and reduce erosion. Others are a river for water and a settlement as a source of labour.

enonce_markdown:
Spot heights were read from a map along the course of a river that flows from a plateau to a plain:

| Distance from source (km) | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Height (m) | 1,300 | 1,240 | 1,120 | 1,080 | 1,070 | 1,068 |

(a) Calculate the average gradient of each 1 km section, as a ratio 1 in n. (b) Identify the steepest section and describe the long profile of the river. (c) Suggest the likely landforms and land use in the first and last sections.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Gradient for a section = height difference : horizontal distance. A steep section is dominated by vertical erosion; a gentle section by deposition and lateral erosion.

### Solution

(a) Height drops: 60, 120, 40, 10 and 2 m per km. Gradients (1,000 m divided by the drop): 1 in 16.7; 1 in 8.3; 1 in 25; 1 in 100; 1 in 500.

(b) The steepest section is the second (1 to 2 km), with a drop of 120 m, which may be an escarpment, rapids or waterfalls. The long profile is concave: steep in the upper course and flattening progressively towards the plain, where the river approaches its base level.

(c) In the first section (1 in 16.7) the river cuts a narrow V-shaped valley with a fast flow; the slopes are unsuitable for farming and are used for forest, grazing or hydroelectric power. In the last section (1 in 500) the river is slow, meanders and has a wide floodplain with swamps; fertile alluvium supports rice and other crops, but flooding limits permanent settlement.
